around.headline: Bengaluru landlord booked for skipping tenant verification
around.summary: A Bengaluru landlord has been booked after failing to verify the identity documents of three tenants who turned out to be undocumented Bangladeshi nationals, per The Times of India. If you're renting out a flat, file the mandatory tenant-verification form with your local police station before handing over keys — cash upfront or a broker's word isn't a substitute.

around.headline: IAS officer suspended over KPSC recruitment scam
around.summary: An IAS officer has been suspended after being implicated in a scam involving the Karnataka Public Service Commission's recruitment process, per The Times of India. Be wary of anyone — including relatives or brokers — who claims they can 'guarantee' a government job for a fee, and report such offers to the Karnataka Lokayukta.

around.headline: Bike ban on Electronics City flyover to hit 25,000 commuters
around.summary: A new ban on two-wheelers using the Electronics City flyover, meant to improve safety on the elevated stretch, is expected to affect around 25,000 daily commuters, per The Times of India, and bikers are now demanding a refund of road tax paid for flyover use. If you commute to E-City on a two-wheeler, plan an alternate route or extra time starting now.

around.headline: Metro Pink Line's first stretch set to open this month
around.summary: The 7.5km Tavarekere–Kalena Agrahara stretch of Bengaluru Metro's Pink Line is likely to open this September, per NDTV and The Indian Express. Commuters on the southeastern belt gain a new option, though an official opening date hasn't been confirmed yet.

around.headline: Karnataka withdraws Parks Amendment Bill after Lalbagh protests
around.summary: The Karnataka cabinet has withdrawn the Parks (Amendment) Bill — which would have allowed commercial use inside public parks like Lalbagh and Cubbon Park — after sustained citizen protests, per Deccan Herald and The Times of India. Residents are calling it a win, though the bill could resurface in revised form later.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: No PoP Ganesh idols this year; illegal unit raided in Dasarahalli
around.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has banned Plaster-of-Paris Ganesh idols this year on environmental grounds, and an unlicensed PoP idol-making unit in Dasarahalli was raided and sealed, per The News Minute and Bangalore Mirror. Buy only clay or other eco-friendly idols this Ganesh Chaturthi to avoid a seized purchase or fine.

around.headline: Delhi tightens security and traffic ahead of BRICS Summit 2026
around.summary: Delhi is preparing for the BRICS Summit 2026 with office holidays, traffic restrictions and heightened security around the venue, per News18. If you're travelling to or through Delhi in the coming days, check restricted routes and build in extra time.

street_smart.title: You're renting out your second flat in Bengaluru. A broker brings you tenants who seem decent and offer six months' rent upfront in cash, but their only ID is a photocopied Aadhaar card, and they're in a hurry to move in today — the broker suggests skipping the police tenant-verification form 'to save time.' Like today's case where a Bengaluru landlord was booked for not verifying the credentials of tenants who turned out to be undocumented, what do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India, Sept 4 — a Bengaluru landlord was booked for not verifying the identity documents of three tenants who turned out to be undocumented Bangladeshi nationals. This landlord-side tenant-verification mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks; the closest recent topic, rental agreement traps (2026-09-01), covered a tenant's deposit dispute with a landlord, not a landlord's own legal exposure for skipping ID checks.
street_smart.situation: The broker has vouched for the tenants before, the cash is real and counted, and delaying means losing the six months' rent to another landlord down the street who won't ask questions.

choices.text: Insist on original ID proof and file the mandatory tenant-verification form with the local police station before handing over keys, even if it delays move-in by a day or two.
choices.feedback: Correct. Bengaluru's tenant-verification norms require landlords to submit a form with tenant ID and photo to the local police station (many stations now accept this online) within a short window of a new tenancy. This is the only step that creates an official record — it's what protects you if a tenant is later linked to a crime or found undocumented, as happened in today's case.

choices.text: Skip the police verification since the broker vouched for them and the rent is paid upfront in cash.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A broker's word and cash in hand say nothing about a tenant's actual identity — that's exactly the gap in today's Bengaluru case, where the landlord's failure to verify tenants left them criminally liable once the tenants turned out to be undocumented. Rent paid on time doesn't undo a legal violation.

choices.text: Accept the photocopied Aadhaar and check the number's format yourself online, treating that as verification.
choices.feedback: Risky. Checking a number's format isn't identity verification — a photocopy can't be authenticated for genuineness or confirm the holder is the person standing in front of you. Only the police tenant-verification process is legally recognised as due diligence.

choices.text: Refuse to rent to anyone who can't produce every document on day one, even if they're clearly willing to complete paperwork within a day or two.
choices.feedback: Risky. This avoids the immediate risk but is needlessly restrictive — many legitimate tenants, including migrants, may need a day or two to gather every document. The safer middle path is to hold the police verification requirement firmly while giving a short, reasonable grace period to complete it.

takeaways: File the tenant-verification form with your local police station (many now accept it online) within 24–48 hours of a new tenancy — this is the step that legally protects you, not the rent being paid.
Always ask for original ID (not photocopies) plus a second document (employer letter, passport, or previous landlord reference) before finalising any tenancy.
Keep certified copies of tenant ID and a signed rental agreement on file indefinitely — they're your evidence if a dispute or police inquiry comes up later, exactly as in today's case.

quiz.question: What did the Karnataka cabinet withdraw this week after citizen protests centered on Lalbagh?
quiz.why: The bill would have allowed commercial leasing inside public parks like Lalbagh and Cubbon Park; its withdrawal followed sustained citizen protests at Lalbagh.

quiz.question: Roughly how many daily commuters are expected to be affected by the new two-wheeler ban on the Electronics City flyover?
quiz.why: Traffic police say the ban is meant to improve safety on the elevated stretch, but bikers are pushing back and demanding a road-tax refund.

quiz.question: Where will Aero India 2027 — the first edition since Operation Sindoor — be held?
quiz.why: Aero India has been held at Yelahanka since 1996; the 2027 edition runs February 8–12, with registrations opening this week.

quiz.question: Which river, originating near Nandi Hills close to Bengaluru, once supplied the city's drinking water before its flow shrank?
quiz.why: Bengaluru now depends almost entirely on the Kaveri, pumped over 100km, since the Arkavathy's flow declined due to upstream encroachment and groundwater extraction.

quiz.question: Which regulator oversees India's stock exchanges and protects investors from market fraud?
quiz.why: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) also regulates mutual funds, IPO listings, and insider-trading enforcement.
